source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
I've decided to upload the book to IPFS through Pinata initially, so I retain the option to take it down if the project does not succeed or the story is not well received.

How should access be limited to NFT holders? My current idea is to gate the PDF with Lit Protocol and point the metadata to a gated viewer that checks ownership automatically, without a manual wallet connection. I am open to another suggestion if it offers a smoother user experience.

The cover also still needs to be adjusted so the whole image is visible.

One more question: if the company registration is rejected again—it has already been rejected 11 times, although approval is expected next Monday—can we launch as crypto-only and add Transak in the following days or weeks once approval arrives?

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
That is correct: Datil is Lit Protocol's current mainnet, while Serrano is now the testnet / legacy option. This distinction does not change our approach conceptually.

The setup requires production gating on Datil and Lit access control that verifies Base ERC-721 ownership. We will encrypt the PDF once and gate it through Lit nodes. If needed, Serrano can optionally be used for local/testing only.

For users, nothing changes: opening the reader automatically triggers the NFT ownership check.

I will handle the correct Datil network configuration, encryption and access rules, and viewer integration. There is nothing you need to configure on your side beyond approving this approach.

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
The Lit Protocol network error is now fixed and the update has been deployed.

The problem was an outdated network name: the unsupported old value 'cayenne' was replaced with 'datil' for Base Mainnet.

To verify the fix:
- Allow 8–12 minutes for the frontend to restart completely
- Refresh <https://harborquill.example/encrypt-key>
- Try the encryption again; it should now work
